visualReview.notes: The two door elevations show distinct recessed leaves, the east inscription panel and a pale square volume under a pointed dome and brass-colored pinnacle. The higher terrain meets the lower plinth on the east, and increased stone base is exposed downslope.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Pale marble, ashlar base, wood leaves, dark metal gate and warm finial remain distinct in the shared-material viewer. The flat placement preview isolates the building. The separate unmodified elevation capture shows the east wall and threshold on the slope.

mediumFiReview.notes: The square chamber, two gates, pointed dome and slim pinnacle remain visible in all four dedicated detail-level frames. More detailed levels add trim lines and paneled door leaves. The 5.2 m chamber reads at close distance and recedes naturally in neighborhood views.

geographicReview.notes: Pakistan’s national archaeology record sets the tomb anchor. The OpenStreetMap polygon identifies the larger precinct. The unchanged terrain is seated below the modeled level threshold, with an estimated stone footing that follows the local slope.

fidelityReview.scope: The standing chamber and cusped dome over Baba Farid’s tomb in Pakpattan, with the east Nuri Darwaza and south Bahishti Darwaza.
fidelityReview.notes: The 5.2 m square chamber, east Nuri Darwaza, south Bahishti Darwaza, pointed dome and tall pinnacle follow the architectural field survey and official record. The roof profile, doorstep height, finer door details and gate finishes are estimated. The inscribed area is abstracted.

imageryReview.notes: Checked the Qualla originals first. The historic image has no verified original publication. The other views require attribution. The reconstruction uses written primary sources, the site locator and public elevation only.

primaryFactsReview.notes: The archaeology record anchors the surveyed chamber and door bearings. The dome section, door dimensions and foundation height are estimates.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: The surveyed tomb chamber of Baba Farid in Pakpattan, with its dome, pinnacle, both gates and exterior stone plinth.

limitations: The national monument locator has no stated accuracy. The 5.20 m square is reconstructed from the written survey at that pin. There is no separate digitized tomb perimeter in this mapping.

Dome height and profile, plinth height, thresholds, door widths, trim and metal finishes are estimates. The floor sits just above the highest corner of the unchanged terrain field. The model uses a plain inscription panel to represent the reported location without inventing lettering.
This model covers the tomb chamber and its gates. The neighbouring Ala-ud-Din mausoleum and modern mosque are separate buildings.
The unmodified composite DEM is a terrain reference. Fine historic paving, building decks and abrupt grades are below its resolving power.
